business.claim: Company claim: Rippling sells an all-in-one workforce-management platform spanning HR, payroll, IT, Finance/Spend, workflows and AI, built on unified workforce data.

Company claim: its product ecosystem includes HRIS, benefits, PEO, HR services, headcount planning, recruiting, performance management, LMS, time and attendance, payroll, IT and finance products; the platform advertises 650+ integrations.

Company claim: Rippling targets businesses managing employees and contractors and offers EOR, global payroll, global contractor payments and contractor-of-record services, including local-currency payroll and global tax filing.
Company claim: named customer examples displayed on its site include Blank Street Coffee, Chess.com, Barry's, Y Combinator, Kleiner Perkins, Clay and CookUnity.

traction.claim: Company claim: Rippling's global page says it is trusted by 25,000+ businesses.
Reuters reported that Rippling served over 20,000 customers in May 2025 and offered more than 20 products across HR, IT and finance management.
Company claim: its current careers page reports 6,000+ global employees, $35B of payroll processed, 30,000 employee devices managed, 600+ app integrations and 3x year-over-year revenue growth.
Company claim: Rippling says 17 Wavemakers were selected from more than 75,000 Rippling admins; the cohort's members each use an average of 13 Rippling products.

CNBC reported that Rippling crossed $1B in annual recurring revenue in 2025 and that CEO Parker Conrad said revenue was growing 78% year over year in April 2026; the underlying 78% figure is a company claim.

team.claim: Parker Conrad and Prasanna Sankar are Rippling's founders; Parker Conrad is CEO, and the company launched in 2016.
Albert Strasheim is CTO and SVP of Engineering; before Rippling he was VP of Engineering at Segment, and earlier held senior engineering roles at D2iQ and Cloudflare.
Eisar Lipkovitz is Chief Product Officer; Rippling says he previously served as CIO of JPMorgan's Corporate & Investment Bank, EVP and Head of Rideshare at Lyft, and spent 15 years at Google.

Matt MacInnis is identified by Rippling as Chief Operating Officer, and the careers timeline identifies Adil Syed as CFO; the timeline says Syed joined from Snap, where he was Head of Strategy and Operations and helped lead Snap's IPO.

Company claim: Wan Agus and Gang Wang joined in December 2025 as SVPs of Engineering; Agus previously was CTO at Credit Karma, while Wang previously was CTO at Nuvei and held senior engineering roles at Stripe and Intuit.

funding.claim: Rippling announced a $450M Series G financing on May 9, 2025, plus agreements to repurchase up to $200M of equity from current and former employees; the company said the financing valued it at $16.8B and named Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford and Y Combinator among participants.
CNBC reported that the $450M round had no lead investor and that the $16.8B valuation was up from $13.5B in a round a year earlier.

Aggregator data: Fireround records $1.847B total raised and lists eight recorded rounds, including $7M in 2017, $45M Series A in 2019, $145M Series B in 2020, $250M Series C in 2021, $250M Series D in 2022, $500M in 2023, $200M Series F in 2024 and $450M Series G in 2025; reconcile this with Rippling's own $1.4B figure on its careers page.
The latest publicly evidenced primary valuation is $16.8B, set in the May 2025 Series G.

financial_signals.claim: Reuters reported that Rippling was not profitable in May 2025, had well surpassed $100M in ARR and continued choosing growth over profitability.
CNBC reported that CEO Parker Conrad said annual revenue growth was well over 30%; CNBC also said The Information had reported ARR above $350M at the end of 2023, up from the prior year.

Company claim: Rippling's careers page currently reports 6,000+ global employees and 3x year-over-year revenue growth; its timeline reports 260 employees onboarded in 2020, indicating substantial headcount expansion, although this is not an audited series.
CNBC reported that Rippling crossed $1B in ARR in 2025 and that Conrad said revenue was growing 78% year over year in April 2026; both are company-reported statements rather than audited revenue.
Conrad told CNBC that Rippling was not planning an IPO in the near future and that the company needed to become profitable before going public; CNBC also reported he had avoided layoffs.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Rippling sued Deel in the Northern District of California in March 2025, alleging a corporate-espionage scheme involving a former Rippling employee and claims including RICO, trade-secret misappropriation, tortious interference and unfair competition; these are allegations, not a final merits finding.

A February 23, 2026 federal order in People Center, Inc. v. Deel denied the forum-non-conveniens, personal-jurisdiction and service challenges and most dismissal requests, while granting in part dismissal of Rippling's state-law claims; the case therefore continued on core federal claims.

The federal docket shows the litigation remained active in October 2026: a September 25 order granted in part and denied in part a motion to dismiss, granted a motion to compel and denied a motion to strike, followed by a joint discovery letter brief filed October 19.

Reuters reported that a former Rippling employee admitted spying for Deel under direction of Deel's CEO in an affidavit made public in an Irish court; this is reported litigation evidence and not a regulatory adjudication against Rippling.

The February 2026 court order recites Rippling's allegations that the former employee accessed and transmitted confidential information from Rippling's Salesforce, Slack and Google repositories; the opened sources did not establish a regulator-confirmed data breach by Rippling.

reputation.claim: Aggregator/review platform Glassdoor currently shows Rippling at 3.6/5 from 1,300 reviews, with 66% recommending it, 80% CEO approval and 75% positive business outlook; category scores shown include 3.0/5 for senior management and 3.0/5 for work-life balance.

A June 2026 Glassdoor review cited low pay relative to workload, poor work-life balance, understaffing, high pressure and high turnover; this is an individual former-employee review, not independently verified company data.

Aggregator/review platform Trustpilot shows a 4.5/5 TrustScore and 2,576 reviews; its recent-review summary is broadly positive about usability and onboarding but notes technical issues, slow loading, complex implementation and complicated timesheets.

red_flags.claim: The Deel corporate-espionage litigation remains active through October 2026, with ongoing discovery and dispositive-motion activity; the allegations and litigation burden merit diligence even though there is no final merits judgment in the opened sources.
Rippling is still described as not profitable and not preparing for an immediate IPO, making the path to profitability and liquidity a material underwriting question.

Reported funding totals conflict: Rippling's careers page says $1.4B+ raised to date, while Fireround's aggregator records $1.847B; the difference should be reconciled against primary financing documents and tender-offer treatment.

Employee reputation signals are mixed: Glassdoor's overall score is 3.6/5 but senior-management and work-life-balance category scores are 3.0/5, and a recent former-employee review alleged understaffing, stress and high turnover.

output.verdict: Rippling presents a strong growth profile: a broad unified HR/IT/Finance platform, 25,000+ businesses claimed on its global page, named enterprise customers, $1B+ ARR reported for 2025, and a $16.8B primary valuation. The closer-look items are profitability and cash needs, reconciliation of public funding totals, the still-active Deel litigation and associated information-security allegations, and whether weaker employee-management/work-life scores constrain execution as the company scales.
